#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The reviewer's harness for ACT-OPERATOR-2's apply.sh (independent review, read-only on every tree).
# It runs apply.sh ONLY against copies inside $W with a planted HOME; it reads the ref copies and the worktree's
# merged code, writes nothing outside $W. Default settings path (no --settings-before/--settings-after): the live form.
set -u
REF=/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-148-act2/.gov-runtime/scratch/ref/ACT-OPERATOR-2
TREE=/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-148-act2
W=/tmp/gov-launch-44uztg4z/claude-1000/op2rev/run
case "$W" in /tmp/gov-launch-44uztg4z/claude-1000/op2rev/*) ;; *) echo "harness: bad W"; exit 9 ;; esac
R=$W/root
D=$R/.gov-runtime/scratch/orchestrator/drafts/operator-2
PH=$W/home
OP=$PH/gov-os-operator
INST=$OP/install
REAL_CHMOD=$(command -v chmod)
REAL_MV=$(command -v mv)
FAILS=0
bad() { echo "UNEXPECTED: $*"; FAILS=$((FAILS + 1)); }
say() { printf '\n== %s\n' "$*"; }

setup() {
  chmod -R u+w "$W" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$W"
  mkdir -p "$D/code" "$R/governance/project/operator" "$OP/queue" "$OP/log" "$W/wrap-chmod" "$W/wrap-mv"
  chmod 0700 "$OP/queue"
  cp -p "$REF/drafts/apply.sh" "$REF/drafts/operator-settings.before.json" "$REF/drafts/operator-settings.after.json" \
     "$REF/drafts/APPROVED.after" "$D/"
  cp -p "$REF/drafts/code/opcommon.py" "$REF/drafts/code/operator_run.py" "$D/code/"
  cp -p "$TREE/governance/project/operator/opcommon.py" "$TREE/governance/project/operator/operator_run.py" \
     "$R/governance/project/operator/"
  cp -rp "$REF/live-install" "$INST"
  find "$INST" -type f -exec chmod 0444 {} +
  chmod 0755 "$INST" "$INST/wall"
  : > "$OP/log/launch.lock"
  printf '# planted owner note\n' > "$OP/CLAUDE.md"
  printf '2026-11-01T10:00:00\texit=0\tplanted\n' > "$OP/log/2026-11-01.log"
  # wrappers for the partial-failure cases (used only where PATH names them)
  printf '#!/bin/bash\nfor a in "$@"; do case "$a" in *.operator_run.py.act-operator-2.*) echo "chmod: planted failure (reviewer harness)" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac; done\nexec %s "$@"\n' "$REAL_CHMOD" > "$W/wrap-chmod/chmod"
  printf '#!/bin/bash\n%s "$@"; rc=$?\nlast="${@: -1}"\ncase "$last" in */install/APPROVED) : > "${last%%/APPROVED}/zz-extra" ;; esac\nexit $rc\n' "$REAL_MV" > "$W/wrap-mv/mv"
  "$REAL_CHMOD" 0755 "$W/wrap-chmod/chmod" "$W/wrap-mv/mv"
}

AP() { HOME="$PH" bash "$D/apply.sh" "$@"; }
t() {  # t <label> <0|nz> <regex or empty> <apply.sh args...>
  local label=$1 want=$2 re=$3; shift 3
  local out rc
  out=$(AP "$@" 2>&1); rc=$?
  printf -- '--- %s [apply.sh %s] exit %s\n%s\n' "$label" "$*" "$rc" "$out"
  if [ "$want" = 0 ] && [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then bad "$label: exit $rc"; fi
  if [ "$want" = nz ] && [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then bad "$label: exit 0 where a refusal was expected"; fi
  if [ -n "$re" ] && ! printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq -- "$re"; then bad "$label: output lacks /$re/"; fi
}
fp() { ( cd "$OP" && find . -path ./log -prune -o -printf '%y %m %p\n' | LC_ALL=C sort; find . -path ./log -prune -o -type f -print0 | LC_ALL=C sort -z | xargs -0 sha256sum; [ -d "$D/backup" ] && ( cd "$D/backup" && sha256sum * ) ) | sha256sum | cut -c1-16; }
snap() { ( cd "$W" && find . -path ./wrap-chmod -prune -o -path ./wrap-mv -prune -o -printf '%y %m %p\n' | LC_ALL=C sort; find . -path ./wrap-chmod -prune -o -path ./wrap-mv -prune -o -type f -print0 | LC_ALL=C sort -z | xargs -0 sha256sum ); }
same() {  # same <label> <fp before>
  local now; now=$(fp)
  [ "$now" = "$2" ] && echo "ok: $1: the install, the operator folder and the backup unchanged ($now)" || bad "$1: something changed ($2 -> $now)"
}
own_check() { ( cd "$INST" && python3 -I -B -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "."); import opcommon as oc; r = oc.approved_state("."); print("approved_state:", r[0], (r[1] or "")[:12], r[2])' ); }

say "setup: the planted world from the copies (default settings path, as live)"
setup
echo "apply.sh sha256: $(sha256sum "$D/apply.sh" | cut -c1-64)"
own_check

say "K1/K2: check, apply, the touched set, a second apply, check, undo, check"
t check-before 0 'install: before \(APPROVED 157a9dc01fca\)' check
t check-before-ready 0 '^check: ready to apply$' check
snap > "$W/../out/s0.txt"
t apply 0 '^state applied$' apply
snap > "$W/../out/s1.txt"
echo "--- the touched set (diff of the whole planted world, before -> after apply):"
diff "$W/../out/s0.txt" "$W/../out/s1.txt"
echo "--- installed files against the drafts:"
cmp "$INST/APPROVED" "$D/APPROVED.after" && echo "ok: install/APPROVED == drafts/APPROVED.after byte for byte" || bad "APPROVED differs from APPROVED.after"
cmp "$INST/opcommon.py" "$TREE/governance/project/operator/opcommon.py" && echo "ok: install/opcommon.py == the tree's" || bad "opcommon.py"
cmp "$INST/operator_run.py" "$TREE/governance/project/operator/operator_run.py" && echo "ok: install/operator_run.py == the tree's" || bad "operator_run.py"
cmp "$INST/operator-settings.json" "$D/operator-settings.after.json" && echo "ok: install/operator-settings.json == the after draft" || bad "settings"
( cd "$INST" && sha256sum APPROVED opcommon.py operator_run.py operator-settings.json && stat -c '%a %n' APPROVED opcommon.py operator_run.py operator-settings.json . )
own_check
[ -d "$INST/__pycache__" ] && echo "note: apply left install/__pycache__: $(ls "$INST/__pycache__")" || echo "note: no install/__pycache__"
t apply-again nz 'not in its before state \(applied\)' apply
t check-applied 0 '^check: already applied$' check
snap > "$W/../out/s2.txt"
t undo 0 '^state before \(undone\)$' undo
snap > "$W/../out/s3.txt"
echo "--- diff after apply -> after undo:"
diff "$W/../out/s2.txt" "$W/../out/s3.txt"
echo "--- diff original -> after undo (what stays):"
diff "$W/../out/s0.txt" "$W/../out/s3.txt"
for f in APPROVED opcommon.py operator_run.py operator-settings.json; do
  cmp "$INST/$f" "$REF/live-install/$f" && echo "ok: undo: $f byte for byte the live copy" || bad "undo: $f differs"
done
t check-after-undo 0 '^check: ready to apply$' check

say "K4: the holds, in the before state (check and apply), each alone"
hold() {  # hold <name> <create command...>; then check and apply must refuse and change nothing
  local name=$1; shift
  "$@"
  local f0; f0=$(fp)
  t "check under $name" nz "" check
  t "apply under $name" nz "" apply
  same "under $name" "$f0"
}
hold freeze touch "$INST/act-in-progress.txt"; rm -f "$INST/act-in-progress.txt"
hold journal touch "$OP/log/journal.json"; rm -f "$OP/log/journal.json"
hold lock touch "$OP/log/operator.lock"; rm -f "$OP/log/operator.lock"
hold queue touch "$OP/queue/20261110T120000-ACT-X.req"; rm -f "$OP/queue/20261110T120000-ACT-X.req"
echo "--- a request file not named *.req (the launcher reads only *.req):"
touch "$OP/queue/20261110T120000-ACT-X.txt"; t "check with a .txt in queue" 0 "ready to apply" check; rm -f "$OP/queue/20261110T120000-ACT-X.txt"
echo "--- a request in queue/taken/ (a launch in flight moved it):"
mkdir -p "$OP/queue/taken/x"; touch "$OP/queue/taken/x/20261110T120000-ACT-X.req"; t "check with a taken request" 0 "" check; rm -rf "$OP/queue/taken"
echo "--- the launch lock held (flock on log/launch.lock by another open file):"
exec 8>>"$OP/log/launch.lock"; flock -n 8 && echo "harness holds log/launch.lock"
f0=$(fp)
t "check under launch.lock" 0 "" check
t "apply under launch.lock" nz 'a launch is running' apply
same "apply under launch.lock" "$f0"
exec 8>&-
echo "--- queue/ missing:"
rmdir "$OP/queue"; t "check with no queue/" nz "" check; mkdir -m 0700 "$OP/queue"

say "K4: the holds, in the applied state (check and undo)"
t apply-2 0 '^state applied$' apply
hold2() {
  local name=$1; shift
  "$@"
  local f0; f0=$(fp)
  t "check under $name (applied)" 0 "" check
  t "undo under $name" nz "" undo
  same "undo under $name" "$f0"
}
hold2 freeze touch "$INST/act-in-progress.txt"; rm -f "$INST/act-in-progress.txt"
hold2 journal touch "$OP/log/journal.json"; rm -f "$OP/log/journal.json"
hold2 lock touch "$OP/log/operator.lock"; rm -f "$OP/log/operator.lock"
hold2 queue touch "$OP/queue/20261110T120000-ACT-X.req"; rm -f "$OP/queue/20261110T120000-ACT-X.req"
exec 8>>"$OP/log/launch.lock"; flock -n 8 && echo "harness holds log/launch.lock"
f0=$(fp); t "undo under launch.lock" nz 'a launch is running' undo; same "undo under launch.lock" "$f0"
exec 8>&-

say "K2: undo against a backup that is not as written"
f0=$(fp)
"$REAL_MV" "$D/backup/SHA256SUMS" "$W/SUMS.aside"; t "undo with no SHA256SUMS" nz 'no backup' undo; "$REAL_MV" "$W/SUMS.aside" "$D/backup/SHA256SUMS"; same "undo with no SHA256SUMS" "$f0"
cp -p "$D/backup/opcommon.py" "$W/oc.aside"; chmod u+w "$D/backup/opcommon.py"; printf '#\n' >> "$D/backup/opcommon.py"
t "undo with backup/opcommon.py changed" nz 'does not match its SHA256SUMS' undo
cp -p "$W/oc.aside" "$D/backup/opcommon.py"; chmod 0444 "$D/backup/opcommon.py"; same "undo with backup/opcommon.py changed (restored)" "$f0"
echo "--- backup/operator-settings.json and SHA256SUMS both changed:"
cp -p "$D/backup/operator-settings.json" "$W/st.aside"; cp -p "$D/backup/SHA256SUMS" "$W/sums.aside"
chmod u+w "$D/backup/operator-settings.json"; printf ' ' >> "$D/backup/operator-settings.json"
( cd "$D/backup" && sha256sum opcommon.py operator_run.py operator-settings.json APPROVED > SHA256SUMS )
t "undo with settings+SUMS changed" nz 'not the before state' undo
cp -p "$W/st.aside" "$D/backup/operator-settings.json"; cp -p "$W/sums.aside" "$D/backup/SHA256SUMS"; same "undo with settings+SUMS changed (restored)" "$f0"
echo "--- backup/APPROVED and SHA256SUMS both changed (APPROVED is checked only against SHA256SUMS before the swap):"
chmod u+w "$D/backup/APPROVED"; printf '\n' >> "$D/backup/APPROVED"
( cd "$D/backup" && sha256sum opcommon.py operator_run.py operator-settings.json APPROVED > SHA256SUMS )
t "undo with APPROVED+SUMS changed" nz "" undo
echo "state now: $(AP check 2>&1 | tr '\n' ' ')"
own_check
t "undo again after it" nz "" undo
ls -la "$INST" | sed 's/^/  /'

say "K4: a partial apply (a planted failure at the second file's chmod)"
setup
t "check (fresh)" 0 'ready to apply' check
out=$(PATH="$W/wrap-chmod:$PATH" HOME="$PH" bash "$D/apply.sh" apply 2>&1); rc=$?
printf -- '--- apply with a failure at operator_run.py: exit %s\n%s\n' "$rc" "$out"
[ "$rc" -ne 0 ] || bad "the partial apply exited 0"
ls -la "$INST" | sed 's/^/  /'
( cd "$INST" && sha256sum opcommon.py operator_run.py operator-settings.json APPROVED | cut -c1-12,65- )
t "check after the partial apply" nz "" check
t "undo after the partial apply" nz "" undo
t "apply after the partial apply" nz "" apply
own_check
ls -la "$D/backup" | sed 's/^/  /'
( cd "$D/backup" && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS )

say "K4: the swap's own after-state not 'applied' (an extra file appears as APPROVED lands)"
setup
out=$(PATH="$W/wrap-mv:$PATH" HOME="$PH" bash "$D/apply.sh" apply 2>&1); rc=$?
printf -- '--- apply with an extra file appearing: exit %s\n%s\n' "$rc" "$out"
t "undo as that message says" nz "" undo

say "K4: other states refuse (check, apply, undo)"
setup
chmod u+w "$INST/brief.md"; printf ' ' >> "$INST/brief.md"
t "check, brief.md one byte more" nz 'neither as ACT-OPERATOR-1 left it' check
t "apply, brief.md one byte more" nz "" apply
t "undo, brief.md one byte more" nz "" undo
setup
touch "$INST/extra.txt"; t "check, an extra file" nz "" check; rm -f "$INST/extra.txt"
mkdir -p "$INST/wall/__pycache__"; touch "$INST/wall/__pycache__/x.pyc"; t "check, wall/__pycache__" nz "" check
own_check; rm -rf "$INST/wall/__pycache__"
mkdir -p "$INST/__pycache__"; touch "$INST/__pycache__/x.pyc"; t "check, install/__pycache__" 0 "ready to apply" check; rm -rf "$INST/__pycache__"
chmod u+w "$INST"; rm -f "$INST/win_toast.ps1"; t "check, a file missing" nz "" check
setup
rm -f "$INST/brief.md"; ln -s "$REF/live-install/brief.md" "$INST/brief.md"; t "check, brief.md a link" nz "" check
setup
mkdir -p "$D/backup"; t "apply with an earlier backup" nz 'backup from an earlier apply' apply

say "end"
echo "harness failures (unexpected results): $FAILS"

**K1, the touched set is exact: pass, with F1.**
- `apply` changes the four files to the stated hashes, each 0444:
  - `opcommon.py` → `e392d8a0…`
  - `operator_run.py` → `fe2e2f42…`

**K2, the undo is real: pass, with F2.**

  - no `SHA256SUMS`;
  - a changed backup file;
  - backup settings that are not the before state;
  - a state other than "applied";
  - any hold.

- The rehearsal log shows the restore (lines 28–33) but none of undo's refusals. My harness covered those.

**K3, the rehearsal is real: pass, with F3.**
- It is a run of this `apply.sh`:
  - `rehearse.sh:65` copies the main tree's drafts into the clone, and the clone's copy is what runs.
  - `apply.sh`'s file time (23:19:30Z) is before the run started (23:29:26Z), and its hash today is the package's.
  - The log itself never prints `apply.sh`'s hash.

  - tests: 183 and 220 passed;

  - the journal;
  - the operator lock;
  - a waiting `*.req` request.
- `undo` refuses under the same four holds and under a held `log/launch.lock`. `apply` refuses under a held `log/launch.lock` too.

- These "other" states all refuse:
  - a changed file;
  - an extra file;

## Findings

**F1 (K1): apply also rewrites `install/__pycache__/opcommon.cpython-312.pyc`.** The check at `apply.sh:145` uses `python3 -I` without `-B`. `undo` leaves the new file behind; it goes stale and Python ignores it, because the restored source's size differs. The live install already has this file from ACT-OPERATOR-1's identical check. The install's own check (S17), the control-file hash and `state()` all skip `__pycache__`. The package's list of touched files doesn't name it.
Ordinary work: yes, because every apply rewrites it (shown by my diff).
Consequence: other — no gate changes; the file is compiled from the approved source.
Scope: in.

**F2 (K2): undo checks `backup/APPROVED` only against `backup/SHA256SUMS`.** Apply writes both into the CTO-writable scratch. If both are changed together, undo swaps all four files and then stops with "after the undo the install is other", a state undo then refuses. My harness shows this: exit 1, then "other" on the next run. A check against the computed before-`APPROVED`, made before taking the lock, would refuse first.
Ordinary work: no, because it needs two matching hand edits in `backup/`, which only apply writes.
Consequence: other — the approved old code and settings are back; the operator is told; the digest shows the `APPROVED` hash.
Scope: in.

**F3 (K3, K5, K7): five wording errors in the package, none affecting a gate.**
- §6: the clone was at `6129d96cd40c`, not `92b725a98`.
- §6: the 7,072 left-out calls are the builder's "no log line" count. Not all are "before the log began": the Monitor call came after.

Consequence: other — each error is neutral or conservative.

**F4 (K4): a failed apply leaves a state that undo refuses, and apply's own message says to run undo.**
- I planted a failure at the second file. It exited through `set -e` with only the tool's own error, and left:
  - `opcommon.py` new and `operator_run.py` old;
  - a temporary file `.operator_run.py.act-operator-2.<pid>`;

- After that, `check` says "other … the CTO rebuilds", both `undo` and `apply` refuse, and the install's own check refuses every launch. The backup is intact and passes its `SHA256SUMS` check.
- When the swap completes but the result is not "applied", apply says `run 'bash apply.sh undo'` (`apply.sh:144`), and undo then refuses. §5 gives no step for a failed apply.

Ordinary work: no, because it needs a failure inside a swap of about 50 ms (a full disk, a kill, or a concurrent write).
Consequence: other — it fails closed until the CTO restores the four files by hand; no work is lost.
Scope: in.

**F5 (K6): §2 overstates what the agent checks in the CTO's file.** §2 says "Nothing is trusted from it but each call's event". In the code, two more things are taken from the file:
- (a) Which logged calls are re-judged and which are only counted as `dropped`. A dropped line's hash is accepted if any log line of the same session has it. The reason is never checked, and there is no limit on how many.
- (b) The event's `cwd`. It is neither in the hash (tool name and input only, `operator_run.py:1151-1154`) nor in the guard's log (`pretooluse.py:186-193`), yet it is passed to the hook (`:1346-1348`).

Ordinary work: yes, because the builder already writes dropped lines (112 in the real set) and every call's `cwd`.
Consequence: other — it misstates the trust boundary; the effect of (a) is F6.
Scope: in.

**F6 (K6): the replay re-judges no call that names the sets root.** The builder writes every such call as a dropped line, to keep sets-root paths out of the file, and the agent never re-judges dropped lines. For a path-map ACT that adds a glob to `sets_root_hidden`, those are exactly the calls the glob can turn. The rehearsal's own class-(a) ACT is this kind: its single dropped call was the only one its glob could reach, so "0 turned" was certain from the start. An over-broad glob would pass the after-check.
Ordinary work: yes, because an honest CTO can write a glob broader than intended, and the builder drops these calls by design.
Consequence: fails open — the after-check passes an ACT it exists to stop. The effect is over-refusal (agents are refused reads they need until the owner's undo line), not a loosening.
Scope: out — this comes from DEC-1108 (2)'s design, the builder's secrecy rule and W2-148's merged code. This ACT neither creates it nor can fix it. It needs a residual row and a CTO rule.

**F7 (K7 a): the check doesn't require the guard log to cover the window.** The package's proposed fix covers only the window's start. A gap inside the window passes the same way: a missing day file, or log lines lost to the guard's 2-second write deadline or to an error (which "never blocks the call"). A set with no logged live calls in its window passes with 0 calls re-judged.
Ordinary work: yes, because the guard's log writes can fail silently under load, and until the log holds 48 hours the CTO's own rule is the only hold.
Consequence: fails open — the replay passes a set that doesn't meet DEC-1108 (2)'s 48-hour premise.
Scope: out — a residual of W2-148's merged code. The ACT only installs it. Today it cannot be reached with the real set before about 2026-11-11 20:02Z, because the Monitor call refuses every set until then, which is later than the 48-hour point.
